items.title: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
items.snippet: Vision-Language Models increasingly rely on textual reasoning to solve advanced multimodal tasks. Despite its effectiveness, this paradigm faces two fundamental limitations. First, relying on textual reasoning alone can limit perceptual ability in vision-centric questions, where accurate answers depend on interpreting task-relevant visual evidence. Second, applying textual reasoning uniformly across inputs overlooks question-dependent variation in both reasoning modality and depth, often producing verbose and unnecessary traces when little logical inference is required. To this end, we propose Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning (AVTR), which introduces visual imagination as a complementary re
items.title_ar: ورقة AVTR حول Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
items.summary_ar: تقترح الورقة AVTR، وهو إطار يضيف visual imagination إلى textual reasoning في Vision-Language Models. تعالج الورقة قيدين: ضعف الإدراك البصري في الأسئلة المرتكزة على الصورة، والتطويل غير الضروري في reasoning عندما لا يلزم استنتاج كبير.
items.why_ar: تقدم نمط تصميم لـ reasoning متكيف في الأنظمة متعددة الوسائط، وهو مفيد لأبحاثك ومشاريع الـ VLM.
items.title_en: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
items.summary_en: The AVTR paper proposes Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning, adding visual imagination alongside textual reasoning in Vision-Language Models. It targets two limits: weak perception on vision-centric questions and verbose reasoning where little inference is needed.
items.why_en: It offers a design pattern for adaptive reasoning in multimodal systems that is relevant to your research output.

items.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
items.snippet: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points. Offline, AnyS1 mines grounded enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills, gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated cont
items.title_ar: AnyS1: System-1 لنقاط القرار في أي agent workflow
items.summary_ar: يقدم AnyS1 إطاراً يحوّل procedural skills الموثقة من البشر إلى نقاط قرار مشتركة وقابلة للتعميم. يقلل ذلك استدعاء الموديل الكبير في كل خطوة، مع خفض التكلفة والـ latency في الـ agents.
items.why_ar: قد يخفض تكلفة الـ agents في أنظمة البنك دون الحاجة إلى hooks خاصة بكل بيئة.
items.title_en: AnyS1: One System-1 for decision points in any agent workflow
items.summary_en: AnyS1 is a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills into shared decision points for agent workflows. Offline, it mines enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills and gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated containers.
items.why_en: It could cut the cost and latency of your agent pipelines by routing routine choices to a lightweight model.

items.title: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
items.snippet: Multimodal tabular learning involves classification and regression on tables combining structured numerical and categorical features with unstructured text and images. These unstructured fields are commonly represented by pretrained encoder embeddings reduced with principal component analysis (PCA). This reduction prioritizes input variance but may overlook information relevant to predicting the target. We introduce LightTAR, a simple, inexpensive method that adapts dimensionality reduction to the prediction task. LightTAR augments the standard PCA representation with a few target-aware features extracted jointly from the final and an intermediate encoder layer using regularized partial leas
items.title_ar: LightTAR: تمثيلات target-aware خفيفة لتعلم الجداول متعددة الوسائط
items.summary_ar: يقدم LightTAR طريقة بسيطة وغير مكلفة لتكييف تقليل الأبعاد مع مهمة التنبؤ، بدلاً من الاكتفاء بـ PCA على embeddings الحقول النصية والصور. يضيف الإطار target-aware features مستخرجة من الطبقة الأخيرة وطبقة وسيطة من encoder باستخدام regularized partial least squares. النتيجة تمثيل أخف للجداول متعددة الوسائط يركز على المتغير المستهدف.
items.why_ar: بيانات البنوك الجدولية الممزوجة بنصوص ومستندات تحتاج هذا النوع من التمثيل لتحسين نماذج التنبؤ بتكلفة حوسبة معقولة.
items.title_en: LightTAR: Light Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
items.summary_en: LightTAR proposes a simple, low-cost method that adapts dimensionality reduction to the prediction target instead of relying only on PCA over encoder embeddings. It augments the PCA representation with target-aware features taken from the final and an intermediate encoder layer using regularized partial least squares. The result is a lighter representation for multimodal tables that focuses on target-relevant information.
items.why_en: Banking tabular datasets mixing text and documents can benefit from this cheap target-aware reduction for prediction models.

items.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
items.snippet: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a score of 75.59, while Piccolo-9B and Piccolo-4B achieve 68.35 and 67.46, respectively. All three rank first on the Private benchmark in their respective model-size categories. Research agents analyze model behavior, construct training data, conduct experiments, and use the results

items.summary_en: The Piccolo team releases a family of multimodal decision models from 0.8B to 27B that co-evolve capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement. items.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
items.snippet: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. We make its construction practical for LLMs through Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (K-FAC) and a factorized projection. We also introduce CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant within th
items.title_ar: CurvDelta: تعديل LLM مع الحفاظ على القدرات العامة
items.summary_ar: يقدم البحث CurvDelta، إطاراً قابلاً للتوسع يدمج قيد الحفاظ على القدرات داخل تعريف تحديث الموديل. يعتمد الإطار على K-FAC وإسقاط مُفكك لبناء فضاء منخفض الانحناء تبقى فيه خسارة الحفاظ شبه ثابتة. كما يقدم CurvLoRA كنسخة low-rank منه.
items.why_ar: يهمك لأنه يعالج فقدان القدرات العامة عند fine-tuning للموديلات المخصصة للبنك.
items.title_en: CurvDelta: Preserving LLM Capabilities During Adaptation
items.summary_en: The paper introduces CurvDelta, a scalable framework that bakes a capability-preservation constraint into the parameterization of LLM updates. It uses K-FAC and a factorized projection to build a low-curvature space where updates barely change the preservation loss. It also proposes CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant.
items.why_en: It directly addresses the loss of general capabilities when fine-tuning LLMs for banking use cases.

items.title: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
items.snippet: Language models can gain capacity at little computational cost from n-gram embedding tables: large tables of learned vectors for short sequences of consecutive tokens, which are looked up and added to the model's input or to its intermediate layers. Recent designs commonly use a separate n-gram embedding table for each layer, which makes the tables costly in memory and prevents layers from sharing what they learn. Sharing a single table, however, gives every layer the same embedding and leaves no room for layer-wise preferences, and it performs poorly in practice. We propose Chorus, in which one set of n-gram embedding tables serves the whole network and every layer reads it in its own way.
items.title_ar: Chorus: جداول n-gram embeddings مشتركة مع تكيف لكل طبقة
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة Chorus، وهي طريقة تستخدم جدول n-gram embeddings واحداً مشتركاً لكل الشبكة، مع تكيف يسمح لكل طبقة بقراءته بطريقتها. الهدف تقليل تكلفة الذاكرة الناتجة عن جداول منفصلة لكل طبقة، مع تحسين أداء المشاركة التي تضعف عادة.
items.why_ar: يفيدك كخلفية عن تصميمات الموديلات الموفرة للذاكرة عند بناء نماذج أو تخصيصها.
items.title_en: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
items.summary_en: Chorus shares one set of n-gram embedding tables across the whole language model while letting each layer read it differently. This targets the memory cost of per-layer tables and the poor performance seen when a single table is simply shared across layers.
items.why_en: Useful background on memory-efficient LLM architecture choices when sizing or customizing models.

items.title: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation
items.snippet: We introduce Faithfulness Video Score (FVSCORE), a neuro-symbolic framework for specification-driven video generation evaluation. Existing evaluators rely on holistic MLLM judgments or vision-language metrics, yet aligning their scores with human judgments and tracing them to specific temporal violations remain open challenges. FVSCORE addresses these limitations by compiling each video into explicit propositions capturing prompt requirements and implicit propositions capturing unstated physical, temporal, and cross-modal constraints. It grounds each proposition using specialized perceptual tools and evaluates the resulting confidence traces with soft temporal operators inspired by Linear Te
items.title_ar: FVScore: إطار neuro-symbolic لتقييم توليد الفيديو
items.summary_ar: يقدم الباحثون FVScore، وهو إطار neuro-symbolic لتقييم الفيديوهات المولدة حسب المواصفات. يحوّل الإطار كل فيديو إلى explicit propositions و implicit propositions، ثم يتحقق منها باستخدام أدوات perceptual متخصصة. يستخدم الإطار soft temporal operators لتتبع الانتهاكات الزمنية وربط التقييم بالحكم البشري.
items.why_ar: تقييم الفيديو المولد يحتاج مقاييس قابلة للتتبع، وهذا يهم من يبني تقييمات لأنظمة multimodal.
items.title_en: FVScore: Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Video Generation Evaluation
items.summary_en: The authors introduce FVScore, a neuro-symbolic framework for evaluating generated videos against specifications. It compiles each video into explicit and implicit propositions and grounds them with specialized perceptual tools. Soft temporal operators then trace confidence over time to locate specific violations and align scores with human judgments.
items.why_en: It offers a traceable evaluation approach that matters if you build evaluators for multimodal generation systems.
